obligation: G074 (50 accepted TPS via graph reduction), G046 (S015 P5 at MODEL level), S031 §4/§17
question: TOKEN_EXECUTION_ATLAS_COUNTS measured 964 -> 756 dispatches/token under the four existing fusion levers. A dispatch reduction that is not a wall-time win is not a win. This times it on the sealed resident.
method: 6 ALTERNATING PAIRS unfused/fused, one process each, --complete-wall --pairs 1, 64 new tokens, max_seq_len 256, same prompt. Alternating so drift is common mode. No lake fill running (pgrep modellake = 0).

correctness_first.a_vacuous_check_I_caught: my first identity check compared two EMPTY files and printed TOKENS IDENTICAL. Both greps had returned nothing because the flags were passed as one shell word. Caught by printing wc -c beside the verdict, not by re-reading the script. A non-empty guard is now in the check. This is the check-that-cannot-fail, in my own one-line verification.
correctness_first.strength: identical GREEDY OUTPUT over 64 tokens, not identical logits. argmax absorbs small numerical differences; this rules out a gross semantic change and is not bit-identity.

THE_RESULT: 21.6% FEWER DISPATCHES BUYS 2.4% WALL TIME. 208 dispatches removed per token saves 0.712 ms of a 30.254 ms token.

and_that_corrects_a_machine_constant_in_.prior: the AirGraph sweep measured ~11 us per WITHIN-command-buffer dispatch and ~157 us per cross-command-buffer submission, on synthetic elementwise kernels
and_that_corrects_a_machine_constant_in_.measured_here: 3.42 us per removed dispatch on the real decoder
and_that_corrects_a_machine_constant_in_.reading: 3.2x cheaper than the synthetic figure. NOT a refutation of the AirGraph number -- different kernels, different regime, and these fusions do more than delete a launch (a concatenated matvec reads the same bytes in one kernel; a fused add+rmsnorm makes one pass over the residual instead of two). So this is a per-REMOVED-DISPATCH cost for THIS fusion set, not a per-dispatch cost in general.

where_the_saving_actually_LANDED.split: 79% of the saving is GPU-side, 17% host-side
where_the_saving_actually_LANDED.why_it_matters: S031 §1 says host overhead is ~1.1% and is not the lever. Host here is 4.29% of wall and the fusion moved almost none of it. The dispatch cost that fusion removes lives on the GPU TIMELINE, not in host submission -- so §1's premise is CONFIRMED and its conclusion is bounded by the next section.

THE_CEILING_THIS_PUTS_ON_THE_DISPATCH_LA.assumption_stated_because_it_is_load_bea: LINEAR: every dispatch costs the same 3.42 us of removable overhead. This is FALSE in detail -- a 2048-row matvec and an argmax do not cost the same -- so these are ESTIMATES under an assumption, not measurements.
THE_CEILING_THIS_PUTS_ON_THE_DISPATCH_LA.CONCLUSION: THE DISPATCH-REDUCTION LADDER CANNOT REACH 50 TPS ON THIS BODY. S031 §4's ladder 964 -> <200 is worth about 36.2 raw TPS, and 50 RAW is above the ceiling of deleting EVERY dispatch. At the capability floor of 30/43 that is 25.2 ACCEPTED TPS against the §19 target of 50 accepted. The reason is arithmetic and was visible in the first measurement: GPU is 95.6% of wall and the bytes still have to move.
THE_CEILING_THIS_PUTS_ON_THE_DISPATCH_LA.what_this_does_NOT_refute: S031 §1 called the execution-graph hypothesis 'the current working mechanism, not yet a universal law'. What is bounded is DISPATCH COUNT as the lever. A graph change that removes BYTES rather than launches -- fusing gate+up so the activation is read once, or consuming a packed representation without a separate unpack -- is a DIFFERENT mechanism this measurement says nothing about, and the decoder being 95.6%% GPU-bound is exactly what makes byte elimination the remaining candidate.

outliers_reported_not_dropped_silently.distribution: 2 fused and 1 unfused, so the outlier process is ARM-INDEPENDENT and does not bias the direction
outliers_reported_not_dropped_silently.they_are_GPU_side: host wall-minus-gpu is 1.14-1.22 ms in all three, indistinguishable from the clean runs; the entire excess is in gpu_ns
outliers_reported_not_dropped_silently.cause: UNKNOWN. Not investigated here. Candidates not tested: thermal, another GPU client, Metal working-set paging of a 9.9 GB resident.
outliers_reported_not_dropped_silently.how_they_are_handled: EXCLUDED from the medians, with the raw table published above so the exclusion is auditable. Including them would put unfused at 30.27 and fused at 29.55 medians anyway -- the direction survives either way, but the 2.4%% figure would not.
outliers_reported_not_dropped_silently.honest_reading: a 25%% outlier rate means this instrument is NOT at the program's own 200-rep standard. n=5 and n=4 clean runs is admitted by COMPLETE SEPARATION and by 0.58%%/0.13%% clean-arm spreads, not by a rep count.

claim_boundary: ONE prompt, ONE artifact, ONE machine, 64 tokens, max_seq_len 256. Dispatch count is prompt-independent; WALL TIME at longer context is not, and no context sweep was run.
NO CAPABILITY SUITE RUN under fusion. 64/64 greedy token agreement is a smoke check, not the S031 §18 floor of 30/43. The fused graph is NOT cleared for the resident until that runs.
The ceiling estimates assume a uniform per-dispatch cost and are labelled ESTIMATES; the 2.4%% and the 3.42 us are MEASURED.
n=5/n=4 after excluding 3 of 12 runs, far below this program's 200-rep gate.
The four fusion levers pre-existed; nothing about any kernel was written or changed in this block.
next: run the 43-case capability suite under fusion (the §18 floor), then attack BYTES rather than launches -- the affine-q2 MLP gate+up fusion that FUSE_MLP does not reach is the one candidate that removes a read rather than a launch
